note.text: Critical AI infrastructure is increasingly governed through closed-door commercial agreements rather than public law, and that shift matters more than any single model release. When procurement contracts and voluntary pledges substitute for enforceable rules, the public loses the ability to audit decisions that shape elections, markets, and courts. Oversight negotiated in private, by parties with commercial interests in the outcome, is not oversight at all. The real infrastructure question is not what these systems can do, but who gets to decide, and in what room.
